questions.question: A large project needs disciplined phases with defined milestones, use-case-driven iterations, and architecture-centric risk reduction, so management chooses Rational's iterative framework instead of pure waterfall. Which process framework?
questions.explanation: RUP organizes development into Inception, Elaboration, Construction, and Transition, iterating within phases - waterfall's structure with iteration inside.

questions.question: A patch fixes a login defect; before release the team re-runs the full 400-case suite over checkout, search, and reports to confirm nothing else broke. Which testing activity is this?
questions.explanation: Regression testing re-executes existing tests after a change to prove unchanged functionality still works - the defect fix must not break the rest.

questions.question: A defense contractor may not begin coding until a review board signs off that requirements and architecture deliverables are complete, and funding for each stage depends on passing its review. Which governance approach is this?
questions.explanation: Phase gates block progression until a phase's deliverables and exit criteria are formally accepted - control via decision points between stages.

questions.question: To clarify vague UI requirements, the team builds a quick clickable mock-up in two weeks, reviews it with users, then discards it and writes the real system on a clean codebase. Which prototyping type?
questions.explanation: Throwaway (rapid) prototyping exists only to elicit and validate requirements; it is deliberately discarded, not hardened into the product.

questions.question: A startup ships a skeletal app to early users, then each release hardens and extends the same codebase until it becomes the production product. Which prototyping type is this?
questions.explanation: Evolutionary prototyping grows the prototype into the final system through successive refinement - the opposite of a throwaway mock-up.

questions.question: Although nothing is broken, the team refactors duplicated logic and upgrades deprecated libraries so future changes stay cheap and faults stay unlikely. Which of the four maintenance categories does this belong to?
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance restructures or updates a working system to head off future faults - unlike corrective fixes or perfective feature work.

questions.question: Before acquiring a codebase, the buyer computes a 0-100 score from cyclomatic complexity, Halstead volume, and lines of code to gauge how cheaply the software can be modified. Which composite metric is this?
questions.explanation: The Maintainability Index blends complexity, volume, and size into a single score estimating how easy a codebase will be to maintain.

questions.question: A moderator schedules the review, a reader paraphrases the code line by line, and a recorder logs every defect against a checklist - the formal review process defined by Fagan. Name it.
questions.explanation: Fagan-style code inspection is the most formal review: assigned roles, preparation, a checklist-driven meeting, and logged defect follow-up.

questions.question: Requirements are signed off, and before coding the architects produce a technical document covering component breakdown, interfaces, data schemas, and algorithms. Which document is this?
questions.explanation: The SDD translates 'what' the SRS specifies into 'how': architecture, component responsibilities, interfaces, and data design.

questions.question: The riskiest element of a project is an unproven third-party payment integration, so the PM schedules a spike and prototype of it in iteration 1 rather than last. Which planning approach orders work this way?
questions.explanation: Risk-driven development tackles the highest-uncertainty items first so catastrophic surprises surface while the budget can still absorb them.

questions.question: A company routes only 5% of user traffic to a new release to detect problems before rolling it out to everyone. What deployment technique is this?
questions.explanation: Canary deployments expose a new version to a small subset of users first, limiting blast radius before full rollout.

questions.question: An e-commerce site keeps two identical production environments and instantly switches all traffic to the updated one after verification. What deployment technique is this?
questions.explanation: Blue-green deployment maintains two identical environments so traffic can switch instantly, enabling near-zero downtime and easy rollback.

questions.question: The four phases of the Rational Unified Process, in order.
questions.explanation: RUP divides each project into Inception, Elaboration, Construction, and Transition phases, each possibly spanning several iterations.

questions.question: A high-risk aerospace project iterates in loops that each set objectives and alternatives, analyze and resolve risks, build and test an increment, then plan the next loop. Name the model and the engineer who proposed it in 1988.
questions.explanation: Boehm's 1988 spiral model drives each cycle by risk analysis rather than a fixed phase list, making it the archetype of risk-driven iteration.

questions.question: For a compliance audit, a multinational must map its acquisition, development, operation, and maintenance activities onto the internationally agreed framework for software life cycle processes. Which ISO/IEC standard defines it?
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 12207 (later ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207) is the reference framework of processes, activities, and tasks spanning the whole software life cycle.

questions.question: In the V-Model, the development phase during which integration test plans are prepared.
questions.explanation: Each V-Model development stage pairs with a test stage: high-level/architecture design pairs with integration testing (as system design pairs with system testing).

questions.question: In Boehm's Spiral model, the activity performed in each loop's second quadrant, right after objectives and alternatives are set.
questions.explanation: Quadrant 2 evaluates alternatives and identifies/resolves risks - typically through prototyping - before development proceeds.

questions.question: The Rational Unified Process phase whose milestone is 'Initial Operational Capability' - the first usable, beta-quality release of the system.
questions.explanation: In RUP, Construction builds out the remaining features and ends at the Initial Operational Capability milestone, before Transition deploys the product.

questions.question: In the V-Model, the development phase during which system test plans are prepared.
questions.explanation: System tests validate the overall system specification, so their plans are written in parallel with the system design stage on the V's left arm.

questions.question: The four quadrants of each loop in Boehm's Spiral model, in order.
questions.answer: Determine objectives and alternatives -> identify and resolve risks -> develop and verify the next-level product -> plan the next iteration
alternatives: 1) objectives & alternatives 2) risk resolution 3) develop & test 4) plan next loop
questions.explanation: Each spiral cycle sets objectives/alternatives, analyzes and resolves risks, develops and verifies that increment, then plans the next loop.
